title: VP of Product Management

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: As a wholesale distributor with 20,000+ SKUs serving sign manufacturers and large-format graphics companies, the VP of Product Management owns portfolio strategy, vendor selection, and product line expansion decisions. This role would care about Tedlar because: (1) Adding a premium protective film with 12-20+ year outdoor lifespan differentiates GSG's offering in a competitive distribution market, enabling them to win higher-margin business from quality-focused sign manufacturers; (2) Tedlar's proven durability and UV protection reduce warranty claims and customer complaints that flow back through the distribution channel, improving GSG's reputation and customer retention; (3) With GSG actively promoting application tapes and overlaminates (RTape partnerships) at ISA Sign Expo, Tedlar represents a natural portfolio extension that complements existing product lines and strengthens their position as a one-stop-shop for premium graphics solutions; (4) The recent Grimco acquisition creates opportunity to establish Tedlar across a combined distribution network, and this role drives those portfolio integration decisions. Their KPIs around gross margin improvement, supplier partnerships, and market share growth align directly with introducing a differentiated, premium-positioned protective film.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: As VP of Product Management at a $207M wholesale distributor with 20,000+ SKUs, [Name] owns strategic decisions about which products GSG adds to their portfolio, which vendor partnerships to pursue, and how to position their offering in the market. They likely evaluate new suppliers based on margin potential, competitive differentiation, and customer demand. [Name] reports to C-level executives (likely CEO or COO) and collaborates closely with Sales, Procurement, and Marketing teams to ensure product line decisions align with revenue growth and market positioning goals. This role has direct authority over product line expansion and vendor selection, making them the primary gatekeeper for introducing Tedlar into GSG's distribution network.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: Given GSG's customer base of sign manufacturers, large-format graphics companies, and vehicle wrap installers, three Tedlar use cases are most relevant: (1) Outdoor signs and graphics protection—GSG customers manufacturing outdoor signage face field failures from UV damage and weathering, and Tedlar's extended outdoor lifespan directly addresses warranty claims that flow back through GSG's distribution channel; (2) Vehicle wrap and fleet graphics overlaminates—GSG serves wrap installers who need protective films that resist graffiti and maintain color integrity across multi-year fleet contracts, where Tedlar's graffiti resistance (spray paint and permanent markers clean off easily) solves a specific customer pain point; (3) Architectural graphics and building wraps—As GSG positions itself as a comprehensive supplier for the graphics industry, Tedlar enables them to serve customers working on premium architectural projects requiring extreme temperature tolerance and weather resistance. These use cases directly benefit [Name]'s team by creating upsell opportunities within existing accounts and attracting quality-focused customers who currently purchase from competitors.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: [Name] likely owns KPIs around gross margin improvement, product line profitability, portfolio differentiation, and customer satisfaction scores. They care about avoiding commodity price competition by offering products that justify premium pricing. A key pain point for this role: When GSG's customers experience product failures or warranty claims with current overlaminate suppliers, those complaints escalate to [Name]'s team, creating service issues and potential account churn. Tedlar's value propositions directly address [Name]'s performance metrics: (1) Higher margins—premium protective films command better pricing than commodity alternatives; (2) Reduced customer complaints—Tedlar's proven durability means fewer field failures and warranty escalations; (3) Competitive differentiation—being able to offer a protective film with demonstrable performance advantages helps GSG win business from quality-focused sign manufacturers who currently buy from competitors; (4) Strategic vendor relationships—partnering with DuPont adds credibility to GSG's portfolio, similar to their existing 3M and RTape partnerships.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: Three timing factors make NOW an optimal moment for outreach: (1) GSG is exhibiting at ISA Sign Expo 2025 (Booth #3325)—trade show preparation creates natural urgency to evaluate new products that can be showcased to attract quality-focused buyers and generate leads; (2) The Grimco acquisition closed in January 2025, and [Name] is likely in active portfolio consolidation and expansion mode, evaluating which products to scale across the combined distribution network—this is the exact window when new supplier relationships are established; (3) GSG actively promotes protective films and overlaminates (RTape partnerships) in their current marketing, signaling that this product category is a strategic priority where they're open to expanding their offering. The combination of trade show deadlines, post-acquisition integration, and demonstrated focus on the protective film category creates a high-relevance moment for introducing Tedlar.

personalization_hooks.hook: GSG already promotes application tapes and overlaminates through RTape partnerships and exhibits at ISA Sign Expo, indicating protective films are a strategic product category
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Position Tedlar as a natural portfolio extension that complements their existing protective film offerings but serves the premium segment where their sign manufacturer customers face the most acute pain points around field failures and warranty claims. Frame it as filling a gap in their current lineup rather than competing with existing suppliers.

personalization_hooks.hook: The Grimco acquisition closed January 2025, creating a window where portfolio decisions and vendor relationships are being consolidated and rationalized across the combined distribution network
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Acknowledge the integration opportunity explicitly: 'I know GSG is integrating with Grimco's operations—this creates a unique window to introduce a premium protective film that could scale across your combined 10-location network and differentiate your portfolio as you consolidate supplier relationships.' This shows you understand their business context and positions Tedlar as a strategic advantage during transition.

personalization_hooks.hook: As VP of Product Management at a wholesale distributor, [Name] experiences customer complaints and warranty issues that originate from product failures at the end-user level, creating service headaches and potential account churn
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Lead with empathy about the downstream impact of protective film failures: 'When your sign manufacturer customers face UV degradation or graffiti damage in the field, those warranty conversations often come back through your team.' Position Tedlar as reducing service escalations and strengthening customer relationships, not just as another SKU to stock.

recommended_approach: Lead with the ISA Sign Expo timing and portfolio differentiation angle. Open by acknowledging their trade show presence and existing focus on protective films, then quickly pivot to how Tedlar fills a specific gap in their current lineup—the premium segment where their customers face the most warranty risk and where GSG can capture higher margins. Position yourself as understanding their distributor business model (you're not selling to them as end-users, but as a channel partner who can help them win higher-value accounts). Close with a low-friction ask to discuss whether Tedlar fits their ISA booth strategy or post-acquisition portfolio expansion plans.
